title: mini-audit search-ledger
description: What the search currently knows, suspects, is blocked on, and intends to investigate next (Search Governance v1, R2-1). This is the research plane, not the finding-verdict plane: agents never write this file. They submit a research delta and the runtime applies it under the Search Governance lock. Semantic keys are the idempotency address — unique across every research kind and the attack graph, not per kind — and identity fields decide conflicts while mutable fields merge.

generation.description: Shared with attack-graph.json and bumped by every `research apply`. Equality across the two files means the last transaction was not interrupted. A mismatch is a fail-closed condition, not something to reconcile silently: the runtime sees a coherent snapshot or refuses to reason at all. Note that writers which legitimately touch only one artifact (an objective revision records a ledger fact but deliberately leaves the graph alone) preserve the value rather than bumping it.

decisions.description: Append-only decision log (spec §5). The runtime canonicalizes entries from delta.decisions into this array. Entries here MUST have a non-empty decision_id; re-applying the same id is a no-op. Agents never write this field directly.

key.description: Author-supplied idempotency address. Re-applying a delta that carries the same key must not create a second object.

claim.description: Identity field. A different claim is a different fact and needs a new key.

diff_evidence_ref.description: Pointer to the diff-scope.json artifact that justifies this fact in an incremental round (the form is 'diff-scope.json:scope_type=…:baseline=…:target=…'). Set by the runtime from a research-delta's diff_evidence_ref. Distinguishes 'changed code' evidence from 'unchanged code' evidence so a resumed audit can tell a stale fact from a current one.

claim.description: Identity field — the security assumption the product depends on.

status.description: supported strengthens every blocker that depends on this claim; disproved reopens them. Mirrored from the fact that an assumption is a first-class object, not a note.

depended_on_by.description: Informational: recomputed by the runtime from blocked paths whose blocker names this assumption. Not the source of truth for reopen decisions.

diff_evidence_ref.description: Pointer to the diff-scope.json artifact that triggered the most recent status change. Set when the assumption moves to 'disproved' or 'supported' in an incremental round, so a later reader can answer 'why did this reopen' without re-deriving it from two bare SHAs.

attempt_refs.description: Paths to execution records proving the question was actually investigated. A deferral with no attempt behind it is not a deferral.

blocked_path_ref.description: Alternative to attempt_refs for a deferral that follows from a still-valid blocker, e.g. a BP- id whose assumption is supported.

candidate_id.description: Identity field. Candidates keep their own author-supplied ids; this is the only pointer between the two id spaces.

claim.description: Identity field. The same candidate can legitimately carry two blockers of the same type, so type alone is not enough.

assumption_ref.description: Identity field when present. An assumption id (A-…) or semantic key that, if disproved, invalidates this blocker.

status.description: A locally real bug that cannot be exploited yet stays 'blocked'. It is never moved to the candidate's rejected status: 'this path is currently obstructed' is not 'this bug is disproved'.

close_reason.description: Written by the runtime when a path closes, e.g. 'blocker_supported'. Closing a path never rewrites the candidate's own status.

derived_events.description: Mechanically-derived facts produced by the runtime (spec §4: 'Runtime may organize facts for the model, but must not evaluate which fact deserves action'). Examples: blocked_path_reopenable, goal_reachable_from_capability, prerequisite_satisfied. The model reads these and decides what to do; the runtime never acts on them.

subject.description: Canonical id of the object the event is about (e.g. 'BP-003', 'CAP-007').

reason.description: Free-form description of why the runtime derived this event.

at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp recorded by the runtime when the event was derived.

delta_ref.description: Optional — the research-delta's key that triggered the derivation.

strategy.description: Identity field — e.g. caller-search, variant-search, capability-consumer-search.

Decision.description: Decision provenance (spec §5). The runtime canonicalizes entries from delta.decisions into this array.

decided_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the runtime stamped at canonicalization time. Agents do not write this; the runtime sets it.

delta_generation.description: The generation number the runtime stamped alongside the decision. Lets an audit trace a decision back to the exact transaction that committed it.
